h1: Ranch Fencing in Valley Mills, TX
heroSub: We build barbed wire, pipe, and game fence for cattle and hay operations along the North Bosque River. Free written estimates on both sides of the Bosque County line.
introHtml:
Valley Mills sits right on the Bosque County line, where the blackland flats give way to limestone hills and the North Bosque River cuts through some of the best grazing ground in Central Texas. Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds ranch fence here for cattlemen and hay producers who need fence that holds stock, survives river-bottom floods, and doesn't need babysitting. We're based out of Waco, about 20 minutes down Highway 6, so we can get a crew to your place fast.

Whether you're cross fencing a hay operation off FM 217, replacing a worn-out perimeter along the river, or hanging a new entrance on Highway 6 frontage, we'll walk the line with you and put real numbers on paper. Every job starts with a free written estimate, and we're licensed and insured. Call us at (254) 555-0184.

services.title: Barbed Wire Fencing
services.desc: Five and six strand barbed wire fence is still the workhorse for cattle around Valley Mills. We drive or drill posts to match your ground, whether that's river-bottom loam or the rocky caliche in the hills west of town.

services.title: Pipe Fencing
services.desc: Welded pipe fence for corrals, working pens, and highway frontage that takes a beating from cattle. Pipe holds up along Highway 6 where wood posts rot out and T-posts get pushed over.

services.title: Game Fencing
services.desc: High game fence for exotics and whitetail operations in the Bosque County hill country west of Valley Mills. We build 8-foot net wire that follows rough terrain without gaps at the bottom.

services.title: Ranch Entrance Gates
services.desc: Custom ranch entrance gates and cattle guards for places off Highway 6 and FM 217. A solid entrance sets the tone for the whole property, and it keeps stock in when a delivery driver forgets to latch up.

sections.heading: Fence Built for Bosque County Ground
sections.html:
The ground around Valley Mills changes fast. East of town toward McGregor you've got deep blackland that swells and heaves, and west of town the limestone starts, where a post hole means a rock drill, not a set of hand diggers. We bring the right equipment for both, so your corners are set in concrete where they need to be and your line posts don't walk out of the ground after the first wet winter.

Along the North Bosque River, flooding is the fence killer. We build water gaps that are designed to break away and get rebuilt cheap, instead of letting a flood take out a quarter mile of good fence. That's the kind of detail that saves you money three years from now, not just on install day.

We also handle brush and cedar clearing on the fence line before we build. A clean right of way means tighter wire, straighter runs, and a fence that's easier to maintain when you're checking it from the truck.

sections.heading: What Ranch Fencing Costs Around Valley Mills
sections.html:
Straight talk on numbers. Around Valley Mills, 5-strand barbed wire typically runs $2.50 to $4.50 per foot depending on terrain, brush, and how much rock we hit. Net wire field fence runs about $3.50 to $6.00 per foot, and full pipe fence runs $30 to $50 per foot for corrals and frontage.

High game fence usually lands between $4.50 and $8.00 per foot, with rocky hill country on the high end of that range. On a long perimeter job, figure a mile of barbed wire fence at roughly $13,000 to $24,000 all in, with corners, braces, and gates driving the spread. For a full breakdown of what moves the price, see our ranch fence cost guide.

Every place is different, which is why we walk the line before we quote. Your written estimate spells out materials, footage, and gates so there are no surprises when the crew shows up.

sections.heading: Storm Damage and Cattle-Out Emergencies
sections.html:
When the North Bosque comes up out of its banks, fence goes down. And when fence goes down, cattle end up on Highway 6, which is a wreck waiting to happen. That's why we run a 24/7 emergency line for storm damage and cattle-out situations at (254) 555-0184.

We'll get out to your place, patch the breach to hold stock overnight, and then quote the permanent repair in daylight. Temporary hot wire, water gap rebuilds, washed-out brace repairs, we've done all of it up and down the river bottom.

We serve the whole area between Waco and the Bosque County line, including neighbors in Crawford and McGregor. If your fence is down tonight, don't wait until morning to call.

faq.q: Do you build fence on both sides of the Bosque County line?
faq.a: Yes. Valley Mills straddles the line between Bosque and McLennan counties, and we work both sides every week. Same crews, same pricing, whether your place is in the river bottom east of town or up in the hills toward Clifton.

faq.q: How do you handle fence across the North Bosque River and its creeks?
faq.a: We build dedicated water gaps at every crossing. They're designed to give way in a flood so the main fence stays standing, and they're cheap and quick to rebuild afterward. It's the only sensible way to fence river-bottom pasture around Valley Mills.

faq.q: What does barbed wire fence cost per foot near Valley Mills?
faq.a: Most 5-strand barbed wire jobs around Valley Mills run $2.50 to $4.50 per foot. Rocky ground west of town and heavy cedar on the line push the price up, while clean, flat blackland runs cheaper. We give you a free written estimate with exact footage and materials before any work starts.

faq.q: Can you fix fence fast if my cattle get out?
faq.a: Call our 24/7 line at (254) 555-0184 and we'll get a crew moving. First priority is a patch that holds your stock overnight and keeps them off Highway 6 and FM 217. Then we come back and quote the permanent fix in daylight.
